CHAPTER / 01

Project Overview

THE CHALLENGE

Design a full suite of interactive booth experiences on a tight timeline — bringing together live hardware, kiosks, cinematic storytelling and immersive theater moments into one seamless journey. The content was dense: recycling policy, material science, machine performance, and service capability all had to feel premium and understandable in a noisy show-floor environment.

THE SOLUTION

We built one connected brand experience with several interactive stops — including the HyPET-6e demo, rPET Knowledge Center, Advantage+ Elite Monitoring Center, and the Tooling Transparent Experience — unified by a shared chapter structure, dual-screen interaction model, and reusable UI system.

02
CHAPTER / 02

Goals Of The Project

  1. 01Make Husky feel modern, premium and memorable
  2. 02Give visitors a clear path through the booth
  3. 03Turn technical information into engaging stories
  4. 04Let multiple conversations happen at once
  5. 05Connect the physical products to the digital experience
  6. 06Make sustainability and performance easier to understand
03
CHAPTER / 03

Process / Experience Structure

01Early Experience Sketches+

We started by sketching the booth as a journey, not a deck. Early wireframes mapped kiosk flow, chapter structure, tap interactions, motion cues, and how each touchscreen stop could talk to the larger booth environment — so sales conversations and self-guided exploration could coexist.

02Dual-Screen Interaction Model+

A consistent dual-screen pattern kept complex content usable on the floor: the upper display carried cinematic visuals and data moments, while the lower touch surface handled navigation, selection, and controls. Flows for geographic zoom, product carousels, video chapters, side-by-side comparison, and factory planning all followed the same hierarchy — reducing learning cost as visitors moved between stops.

03Screen Flow + Prototype Structure+

Each chapter was prototyped as a paced screen flow so the team could review transitions, content hierarchy, and dwell time before production. That structure made dense topics — advocacy, global rPET adoption, life of rPET, selection, comparison, and best practices — feel like a guided story instead of a data dump.

04UI Component System+

A reusable component library kept every chapter visually and interactively consistent: chapter menus, media players, data cards, gauges, round CTAs, carousels, countdown states, icons, and status indicators. Building the system first meant new content could ship faster without breaking the HUD language that made the experience feel cohesive across the booth.

04
CHAPTER / 04

Art Direction / Visual System

The visual system borrowed from industrial command interfaces — dark surfaces, precise framing, hazard-stripe accents, and high-contrast yellow/cyan highlights — so sustainability and machine performance felt tangible, technical, and premium on a busy show floor.

01Chapter Storytelling+

Chapter intros, lifecycle sequences, comparison layouts, and real-world results screens translated specialist content into scannable moments. Photography, motion, and data visualization were paired so visitors could grasp the story quickly, then go deeper when a conversation started.

02Physical-To-Digital Continuity+

Interaction design extended beyond glass. Tangible cues — place, rotate, select — linked physical product moments to on-screen storytelling, reinforcing Husky’s message of sustainability without compromise in a way visitors could feel as well as see.

05
CHAPTER / 05

Why It Worked

The experience succeeded because process and system design came before polish: a clear visitor path, a shared interaction model, and a componentized UI made complex industrial storytelling feel intuitive under show-floor pressure.

01

What Visitors Could Do

Explore global policy and adoption data, follow the life of rPET, compare material pathways, review best practices, and move between cinematic upper displays and hands-on controls without relearning the interface at every stop.

02

What The System Unlocked

Sales teams could run parallel conversations. Content teams could extend chapters without redesigning the interface. And the brand presentation stayed consistent from LED canopy moments to kiosk-level detail — turning a dense product story into a memorable booth journey.
